completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed three discovery-correctness defects in the literature extension's discover pipeline: silent Tier 3 failure now emits a visible TIER3_STATUS notice surfaced at both the script and /literature command layers; Tier 1 no longer starves Tiers 2/3 via reserved per-tier quotas with rollover; and query-construction noise from multi-paragraph task descriptions is reduced via title-primary/description-capped term construction plus a multi-term match-strength threshold. All 5 plan phases completed; all edits confined to agent-system/extensions/literature/**.

memory_candidates.content: Pattern for fixing 'first-tier-wins' truncation bugs when multiple independently-capped sources feed a shared array before a final head-of-array slice: compute an even-with-remainder per-source quota that sums to the total limit, derive each source's actual contribution from the SHARED accumulator's length (not a per-source local counter, which breaks under dedup), and roll the shortfall forward into the next source's quota before it runs. Makes the final slice a safety net instead of the real selection mechanism. Origin: literature-discover.sh's three-tier discovery pipeline (Tier 1 offline index / Tier 2 Zotero / Tier 3 Semantic Scholar).

awk word-count/field-cap idioms (`for (i=1; i<=NF && i<=n; i++)`) reset NF and the loop per INPUT LINE, not per whole input. Applying such a cap to text that may contain embedded newlines (e.g. a multi-paragraph task description) silently caps EACH line independently instead of the string as a whole, producing far more output than intended. Flatten newlines to spaces (`tr '\n' ' '`) before piping into such an awk script.
